subject: Follow-up: Redwood demo + procurement/billing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme-logistics.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood demo + procurement/billing next steps

Hi Jordan and Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — I appreciated the thoughtful questions from both product and procurement. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Commercial path: agreed POC on card for initial pilot (low friction). For production we discussed moving to a PO with invoicing and net terms.
- Procurement asks: Acme needs an official invoice with PO number, W9/vendor info, and the billing address shown on the invoice. They also asked about net terms and whether we support marketplace (AWS) purchases.
- Action items:
  1) Jordan/Priya: confirm preferred billing contact and billing address, and whether Acme will provide PO for production. Also let us know if VAT/Tax ID is required for invoicing.
  2) Marissa/Rishi (Redwood): provide draft Order Form and W9 for vendor onboarding, and confirm standard net terms and flexibility.

Attached is a draft Order Form to speed the process (redwood_order_form_draft.pdf) and our W9 (acme_w9.pdf).

If it helps, we can support the following options: pay-by-card for pilots and low-dollar purchases (we accept P-cards), or PO with invoice and net terms for production. Standard net terms are net 30; we can consider net 45/60 for strategic deals pending finance approval. If you prefer marketplace procurement, we can discuss AWS Marketplace or a cloud marketplace listing as an alternative (that path has different invoicing/fulfillment).

Please share the billing contact and any required invoice fields (PO number format, billing address, tax/VAT details) and I will get you a formal order form and next steps.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme-logistics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo + procurement/billing next steps

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A couple quick clarifications from procurement: 

1) Net terms: Finance prefers net 45 or net 60 for new vendors, but procurement will accept net 30 if signed off by business. Would Redwood be able to offer net 60 pending enterprise approval?

2) Payment method: We can use P-card for purchases under $25k, otherwise we require a PO. Pilot will likely be under the threshold but production will need a PO.

3) Invoice format: We need a PDF invoice that includes a PO number field, invoice number, billing address, tax ID/VAT, and our vendor code (I will share once vendor setup is complete). Billing address below:

Acme Logistics Inc.
Accounts Payable
500 Harbor Way
Oakland, CA 94607
USA

4) Marketplace: Is Redwood currently listed on AWS Marketplace? If so, can we purchase via marketplace for faster vendor onboarding?

I'll follow up with our AP contact and vendor code. For now please confirm if net 60 is possible and whether you need anything else to start vendor setup.

Best,

Jordan Miller
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Logistics
jordan.miller@acme-logistics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme-logistics.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood demo + procurement/billing next steps

Thanks Jordan — that billing address is perfect and very helpful. Quick answers below: 

- Net terms: Our standard is net 30. We can escalate and submit for finance approval for net 45 or net 60 for strategic customers. To move that along I can open an approval request once you confirm estimated annual spend and pilot timeline (helps our finance justification).

- Marketplace: We are evaluating AWS Marketplace and have a private offer process; we can support purchases via marketplace in many cases but timing for listing varies. If a marketplace purchase is preferable, we can loop in partnerships to discuss timelines and implications for invoicing.

- Invoice format: We will provide a PDF invoice that includes PO number, invoice number, billing address, tax ID, and any vendor code you provide. Please send the vendor code when available.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jordan/Priya: confirm estimated pilot value and target go-live to help us with the net-terms approval.
2) I will open a finance approval ticket for net 45/60 and share the draft Order Form adjusted with Acme billing details.
3) Once PO/vendor code is available we will update the order and issue the invoice.

Attaching the draft order form and W9 again for AP (redwood_order_form_draft.pdf, acme_w9.pdf). Let me know the vendor code when you have it and I will proceed with the approval flow.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a short call with procurement if that helps.

Thanks,

Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme Logistics - net terms request and billing info (DF-12874)

Rishi / Lauren, quick internal note on Acme (deal DF-12874):

- External ask: Jordan asked whether we can offer net 60 for onboarding. Billing address and AP details provided; they will use P-card for pilot (under $25k) then PO for production.
- Pilot estimates: Jordan said pilot likely under $15k; production expected to scale.
- Attachments we sent: draft Order Form and W9.

Recommendation: Approve net 45 as a standard concession; escalate net 60 only if procurement commits to annual minimum and legal signoff (we can capture via the Order Form). Approving net 45 will materially reduce friction and is within our typical stretch for strategic customers. If you approve net 45 I will update the Order Form and push for vendor setup; if you want net 60 we should require an estimated annual commitment in the order.

Let me know your guidance and whether you want me to include a payment schedule or SOW to codify commitments.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
